text.p: Italian bonds and futures slipped lower in early trading following the lower trend to German bunds, but traders expected the market to stabilise around these levels with the focus on government welfare talks.
The lower overnight close to U.S. T-bonds and the easier lira which slipped off Monday's highs also contributed to the continuation of the easier trend to BTP futures seen in late trading on Monday.
"There's a lack of volume out there with futures just watching bunds, while the market's focus continues to be on the welfare talks," said one LIFFE trader.

In a meeting between the Italian government and trade union leaders late Monday, ahead of talks on reforming the country's pensions system, the government said it wanted to cut pension spending by some five trillion lire and overall welfare spending by some seven trillion lire.
Dealers said that bigger cuts in spending had been expected and JP Morgan in a research note on Monday said welfare spending needed to be cut by 10 trillion lire.
Data showing Italian May wholesale inflation falling 0.2 percent year-on-year and producer prices rising 1.1 percent year-on-year for the same month had little market impact.
The lira, after hitting new highs of below 970 lire/mark on Monday, drifted off such firm levels and was last quoted in the 972.00 lire/mark area around 0745 GMT.
